to:

  const seen = (holder.seen ??= new Set<string>());
why: a language seen by an earlier call is never listed again, so the second call on one text answers []; killed by the two-call row and by every enumerated document after the first that shares a language with an earlier one

name: S08 languagesInMarkdown: the Set is an object with `in` (inherited names are always seen)

  const seen = { has: (k: string): boolean => k in table, add: (k: string): void => void (table[k] = true) };

name: S11 languagesInMarkdown: the scan stops at 4,096 distinct languages

name: S12 languagesInMarkdown: the answer is the Set spread (the same list: a Set keeps insertion order)
